stem: Which of the following characteristics accurately distinguishes a tension-type headache from a migraine in pediatric patients?

options.text: Tension-type headaches are not worsened by physical activity.
Tension-type headaches are primarily caused by muscle contractions.
Tension-type headaches are frequently associated with intense photophobia.

explanation: Unlike migraines, physical exertion does not exacerbate the pain levels of a tension-type headache.
rationale: Think about how movement or exercise impacts the intensity of the pain.

optionExplanations.A: Unlike migraines, physical exertion does not exacerbate the pain levels of a tension-type headache.
optionExplanations.B: The source clarifies that abnormal scalp muscle contraction is no longer thought to be the cause; it is likely genetic.
optionExplanations.C: These headaches are classically described as a tight pressure around the head, whereas migraines are more often unilateral.
optionExplanations.D: Sensitivity to light and noise is typically less intense or absent in tension-type headaches compared to migraines.

source.hint: Think about how movement or exercise impacts the intensity of the pain.
